$comment: Self-review config: the dispatcher engine reviews its OWN changes. Tuned for a pure-stdlib GitHub Action with a money path (cost accounting) and a security path (HMAC-signed verdicts, secret redaction).
project_description: The multi-tenant AI peer-review dispatcher engine itself. It is a pure-stdlib GitHub Action (no third-party imports in scripts/dispatcher — enforced by tests/test_dispatcher_standalone.py). It accounts AI spend against per-PR and 24h ceilings (a money path), and trusts only HMAC-signed verdicts authored by the operator/bot (a security path). The front_door/ directory is a separate, portable web app (not the engine).
review_guidance: Stdlib-only violations: any third-party / cross-package import added under scripts/dispatcher (breaks portability; the standalone test guards this).
Money-path errors: cost accounting that double-counts, under-counts, or lets a wrong price/model silently inflate the 24h ledger and trip ceilings.
Identity/verdict bypass: anything that would let an unsigned or non-operator comment count as a verdict or an OPERATOR command (HMAC, author-id checks).
Secret leakage: an API key or webhook URL that could reach a PR comment without passing through redact().
GitHub rate-limit regressions: re-introducing per-PR calls in the sweep, un-memoized issue scans, or retrying a write that could double-post.
Escalation-logic correctness: a converged PR escalating redundantly, or a head-lock / daily-ceiling stop being silently skipped.
